lessonsIntro: Caswell is one of the easiest Gower beaches to learn on, with a car park close to the sand, summer lifeguards and a year-round surf school.

text: Caswell Bay is a small, south-west facing cove backed by cliffs, about half a mile long, between Mumbles and Pennard. Visit Wales picks it out as a good spot for young surfers because the car park is close by, lifeguards patrol in season and the water is clean. SurfGSD teaches here all year, with junior, family and taster sessions, so it is a natural first stop if you are staying around Swansea.

The bay gets small and crowded around high water, so lower and mid tides give you more room. Swansea Council warns of a rip current here, and RNLI lifeguards cover the beach daily from early May to mid-September, 10am to 6pm, plus the Easter holidays. Outside those dates there is no patrol, so learn with a school and stay between the flags when they are up.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Great for juniors and beginners
cards.text: A compact bay with lifeguards in season and a school on the beach, recommended by Visit Wales for young surfers.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Lower and mid tide
cards.text: Avoid high water, when the beach shrinks and gets crowded. Lessons run all year; lifeguards patrol from May to mid-September.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rip current and crowds
cards.text: The council warns of a rip at Caswell. Use the patrolled zones in season and give swimmers space at busy times.

hireIntro: You can hire kit at Caswell itself through SurfGSD, and Hot Dog Surf Shop in nearby Kittle rents boards, wetsuits and bodyboards.

text: Caswell's waves are usually small to medium, so a soft-top is ideal for learners and a mini-mal or longboard suits improvers. Bodyboarders and swimmers use the red and yellow flagged zone when lifeguards are on duty. The water follows the same seasonal pattern as the rest of Gower, so a winter suit with boots and gloves is essential from late autumn. The bay is also popular with paddleboarders and kayakers on flatter days.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Soft-top for learners
cards.text: A wide foam board handles Caswell's whitewater best. Improvers can try a mini-mal on mid-tide days.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 in summer, 5/4 in winter
cards.text: Gower water peaks at roughly 14-18°C in mid-August and drops to about 8-9°C around March. A 3/2 or 4/3 with boots suits summer; from late autumn to spring go for a 5/4 or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards and SUP
cards.text: Bodyboard between the red and yellow flags in season. The council notes the bay is popular with paddleboarders and kayakers too.

shopsIntro: There is no surf shop on the beach at Caswell, but Hot Dog Surf Shop in Kittle is a short drive away on the Pennard road.
shopsText: Hot Dog Surf Shop is at 26 Pennard Road in Kittle, a short drive west of Caswell, with free parking. It sells boards for beginners up to experienced surfers, wetsuits from several major brands, bodyboards and accessories, and has a second-hand board rack. At the beach itself you will find the Surfside café and kiosks selling snacks and beach toys.

lessons.q: Who teaches surfing at Caswell Bay?
lessons.a: SurfGSD runs lessons at Caswell all year, including junior sessions in the school holidays, family sessions and taster days, with all surf kit provided.
RNLI lifeguards patrol daily from early May to mid-September, 10am to 6pm, and over the Easter holidays. Check the RNLI page before you go, as dates can change.

lessons.q: When is the best time to surf Caswell?
lessons.a: Lower and mid tides give more beach and less crowding. Around high water the bay becomes small and busy.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard at Caswell?
hire.a: SurfGSD is listed as offering board hire at Caswell, and Hot Dog Surf Shop in Kittle rents surfboards, wetsuits and bodyboards.

hire.q: Can I bring my dog to Caswell?
hire.a: Not in summer. A seasonal dog ban runs from 1 May to 30 September.

shops.q: Where is the nearest surf shop to Caswell?
shops.a: Hot Dog Surf Shop on Pennard Road in Kittle is the closest dedicated surf shop we found, a short drive away with free parking.
